label: Sequence started with m: late original phase and <DEL> (t>=3)
explanation: Fires on the original-phase steps from t=3 onward and on the <DEL> step of sequences whose FIRST original token is m (first_tok=m: 22.6x lift, 94% of activation mass). It is silent at t=0-2 and silent throughout the copy phase. Activation is weak at t=3 and rises to a plateau around t=5-7, then drops somewhat at <DEL>. The top activations are almost all sequences starting with m m. The current input token has little effect. The missed activations are faint (about 6% of mass) and come from sequences with m at position 1 instead of position 0 (e.g. p m j h y ...). Most false positives sit at t=3, where the activation is just above zero.

issues: Minor overclaim: 'top activations are almost all m m' is true only for the very top examples in the profile. first_tok=m & orig(1)=m covers just 7.5% of the top activation quartile (dev) and has only 2558 predicted steps, so most strong activations come from sequences that start with m followed by some other token. A better wording is 'the very strongest examples start with m m'.

Recall is 0.755 but the misses are faint: they hold 5.7% of activation mass on test. Most missed steps (dev recall 0.181 of the 0.245 missed) are sequences with m at position 1, as the explanation says. That class has low precision on its own (P=0.241, 5.1% of mass), and adding it lowers F1: (first_tok==m | orig(1)==m) & t>=3 & phase<2 gives test F1 0.741, and a gated variant gives test F1 0.793, both below 0.85. So it is a faint secondary pattern, not a fixable gap.

Checked claims: never fires at t<3 or in the copy phase (P=R=0 for both). <DEL> with first_tok=m: P=0.983, 19% of mass. False positives cluster at t=3: precision 0.892 at t=3 vs 0.997 for t>=4, and t=3 holds only 8% of mass, which fits the 'weak at t=3' claim. in_tok lift is flat at about 1.0x apart from <DEL>. Test scores reproduce: P 0.973, R 0.755, F1 0.850, mass recall 0.943.
